stem:
Pihu plans to spot Mars from her open balcony at 8:15 p.m. Mars is above the horizon for her place and date, but thick fog covers the whole sky and a bright porch lamp stays on.

Which judgment is best?

options.text: She is unlikely to see Mars clearly because fog and the bright lamp block a clear dark view.
She will see Mars clearly because it is above the horizon at that clock time alone.
Switching the porch lamp brighter will make Mars easier to find through the fog.
Mars can be seen tonight from every place on Earth under these same clock conditions.

teacher.key_rationale: Visibility needs a clear enough dark sky as well as the object being above the horizon. Fog and bright light block the view; more light makes it worse; place on Earth also matters.
